{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Master Services Agreement

**To:** Deal Team 
**From:** In-house Counsel (Customer-side) 
**Re:** Playbook review of Vendor's Master Services Agreement draft 

---

## Executive Summary

We have completed our playbook review of the Master Services Agreement. Of the 19 rules assessed, **8 clauses deviate** from our positions and **11 are compliant**. The compliant set is genuinely strong: IP and Customer Data ownership (§§ 14.1–14.4, 13.2), assignment and change of control (§ 24), Customer-side termination for convenience (§ 9.4), audit rights (§ 22), renewal mechanics (§ 8.2–8.3), governing law and venue (§ 28), Vendor insurance (§ 18) and the absence of any MFN, non-solicit or liquidated damages burden on Customer all meet our preferred position.

The deviations, however, are concentrated in the most consequential commercial and risk provisions, and several sit squarely in walk-away territory:

- **No Vendor indemnity exists anywhere in the Agreement**, paired with a one-way, unlimited Customer indemnity for Vendor covering "every claim relating in any way to Customer's use of the Services" (§ 20.1).
- **The liability cap is one month of Fees actually paid, "without exception"** (§ 21.1), which is below our floor and neutralises the Excluded Claims regime in § 21.3.
- **A three-year, USD 2,000,000-per-year take-or-pay commitment with no reduction or termination rights** (§ 2.1), a **full-term sole-and-exclusive supplier obligation** (§ 2.2), and a **24-month worldwide post-term non-compete** (§ 12.4) — each of which directly contradicts § 12.3, in which Vendor acknowledges Customer has made no such commitments.
- **§ 11.1 requires immediate cessation of all assistance and permanent deletion of Customer Data** with no export or migration path, contradicting §§ 11.2 and 11.3.
- The **Services licence in § 13.1** runs to "Customer alone", excludes Affiliates and contractors, and is revocable at Vendor's sole discretion — inconsistent with the paid-up licence protections in §§ 13.2–13.3.
- The **conformity warranty period is fifteen days** (§ 19.2), below our 90-day fallback floor, and cuts off the § 19.4 remedies.

A notable feature of this draft is internal inconsistency: § 12.3 disclaims exactly the exclusivity, minimum-volume and non-compete commitments that §§ 2.1, 2.2 and 12.4 impose, and § 11.1 conflicts with §§ 11.2–11.3. Several of our edits simply align the operative grants with Vendor's own acknowledgements. We also note that § 9.3 cross-refers to remedies "required by Section 20.5", a section that does not exist in the current draft.

---

## Findings Table

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section |
|---|---|---|---|
| Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Deviation | § 20 / § 20.1 (with §§ 19.4, 21.3, 30.5) |
| Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability: cap, mutuality, carve-outs | Deviation | § 21.1 (with §§ 21.2, 21.3, cl. 1.5) |
| Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Compliant | §§ 14.1–14.4, 13.2, 15.1 |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity obligations binding Customer | Deviation | § 2.2 (contradicts § 12.3) |
| High | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase / volume commitments | Deviation | § 2.1 (contradicts §§ 12.3, 9.4) |
| High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete restrictions on Customer | Deviation | § 12.4 (contradicts § 12.3) |
| High | TRANSITION — Post-termination transition and data return | Deviation | § 11.1 (contradicts §§ 11.2, 11.3) |
| High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Deviation | § 13.1 (cf. §§ 13.2, 13.3) |
| High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Compliant | §§ 24.1–24.4, 13.3 |
| High | LD — Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer | Compliant | § 9.4 (with §§ 27.3, 7.3) |
| High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Compliant | § 9.4 (with §§ 9.1–9.3, 9.5, 10.1–10.2, 8.2, 27.3) |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Deviation | § 19.2 (cf. §§ 19.1, 19.3, 19.4) |
| Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | §§ 22.1–22.3 |
| Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant | §§ 28.1–28.3 |
| Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation obligations | Compliant | § 12.3 (with §§ 7.1, 8.3) |
| Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation of employees | Compliant | § 12.3 (with § 30.1) |
| Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window | Compliant | §§ 8.2, 8.3 |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Compliant | §§ 18.1, 18.2 |

---

## Walk-Away Items

The following findings were assessed as falling in walk-away territory under the playbook. Each must be resolved before signature.

1. **Indemnification (§ 20.1) — Critical.** No Vendor IP indemnity exists anywhere in the Agreement, combined with an unlimited one-way Customer indemnity for Vendor covering Vendor's own services. This fails both the fallback and preferred positions.

2. **Liability cap (§ 21.1) — Critical.** A one-month cap on Fees *actually paid* sits below the 12-month fallback floor, and "without exception" overrides § 21.3, pulling indemnities, confidentiality, data protection and security, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement inside an illusory cap.

3. **Minimum commitment (§ 2.1) — High.** A three-year, USD 2,000,000-per-year take-or-pay expressly "without reduction or termination rights": no 12-month limit, no 30-day reduction right, no true-up, and a shortfall that operates as a penalty.

4. **Exclusivity (§ 2.2) — High.** A full-term sole-and-exclusive-provider obligation with no category limit, no 12-month cap and no automatic exit for service-level or delivery-date failures.

5. **Non-compete (§ 12.4) — High.** A worldwide, 24-month post-term non-compete of undefined scope, with no carve-out for internal development or acquisitions.

6. **Transition and data return (§ 11.1) — High.** Immediate cessation of all assistance and permanent deletion of Customer Data with no export or migration support.

7. **Services licence (§ 13.1) — High.** Grant to "Customer alone", excluding Affiliates and contractors with no path to add them, non-transferable, and revocable at Vendor's sole discretion.

---

## Next Steps

1. **Issue the redlined draft** covering the eight deviations, with the following proposals:
   - **§ 20:** add Vendor defence and indemnity for third-party IP infringement, Vendor's breach of Applicable Law, Vendor-caused unauthorised access to Customer Data, and Vendor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct, with notice, control-of-defence and cooperation mechanics; narrow Customer's indemnity to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.
   - **§ 21.1:** re-base the cap to the greater of 12 months' Fees paid or payable measured to the claim and USD 1,000,000; replace "without exception" with an "Except for Excluded Claims" hook; extend the payment carve-out to Customer's payment obligations for undisputed amounts due, expressly including taxes, expenses and interest (retaining the Customer-favourable "undisputed" qualifier). § 21.2 untouched.
   - **§ 2.1:** delete the take-or-pay and confirm no minimum purchase or volume commitment; Customer pays only for usage or ordered Services, consistent with § 7.1.
   - **§ 2.2:** convert to a non-exclusive appointment with no sole-supplier obligation, aligning with § 12.3.
   - **§ 12.4:** convert to an express confirmation that Customer is free to compete, aligning with § 12.3.
   - **§ 11.1:** replace immediate cessation and deletion with an expiry-or-termination trigger, up to six months' transition assistance at Vendor's then-current rates, and return of Customer Data within thirty days — leaving §§ 11.2 and 11.3 (machine-readable return format; officer-certified deletion) intact.
   - **§ 13.1:** extend the grant to our Affiliates and to contractors acting on our behalf, replace at-will revocation with the uncured material breach standard already in § 13.3, and delete "non-transferable" to remove the conflict with the § 13.3 transfer right.
   - **§ 19.2:** extend the conformity period to ninety (90) days, apply it to software as well as Deliverables, and delete the fifteen-day cut-off of correction and refund obligations.

2. **Prepare fallback positions** where sensible. On indemnity, if Vendor prefers the fallback structure we can accept the usual exclusions (Customer modifications, combinations, specifications), procure/modify/replace/refund remedies inserted as § 20.5, and a 3× annual fees super-cap. On warranty, § 19.2 as redlined lands at the fallback; we are not pressing the preferred twelve-month software period.

3. **Flag the drafting defect** in § 9.3, which cross-refers to remedies "required by Section 20.5" — a provision that does not exist in the current draft. Our indemnity redline can supply it.

4. **Raise the internal inconsistencies** with Vendor as a package: § 12.3 disclaims the very exclusivity, minimum-volume and non-compete commitments imposed by §§ 2.2, 2.1 and 12.4, and § 11.1 contradicts §§ 11.2–11.3. Aligning the operative grants with Vendor's own acknowledgements should be presented as a clean-up rather than a negotiation.

5. **Confirm no re-trade on compliant provisions.** We will not reopen IP (§ 14), assignment (§ 24), convenience termination (§ 9.4), audit (§ 22), renewal (§ 8.2–8.3), governing law (§ 28) or insurance (§ 18). Minor sub-elements noted for the record only: the § 14.2 payment condition on Deliverable ownership; the § 15.1 "as permitted by this Agreement" processing hook; the § 24.2 reasonableness standard omitting "conditioned or delayed"; and the § 24 competitor bar qualified by "without Customer's consent".

6. **Escalate for business sign-off** on the walk-away items, in particular §§ 2.1, 2.2 and 12.4, which have direct commercial and strategic consequences beyond legal risk allocation."}
